title: Deferred Canary Nerve Center: safe rollout and rollback for batching/caching recommendations
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a 'nerve center' orchestration layer that safely applies Optimize recommendations (batching and KV/prefix caching configs) using deferred canaries, ramp controls, observable checkpoints, and explicit approval hooks. This ticket covers the controller, decision logic, and operational playbook needed to push config changes with automatic rollback triggers and operator override.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can enqueue an Optimize suggestion and create a staged rollout with 4 phases (dry-run, 1%, 25%, 100%).
Each phase exposes metrics slices (latency p50/p95, token cost, error rate, model score drift) for comparison against baseline within the Console dashboard.
Automatic rollback executes when any safety invariant flips (config mismatch, latency increase > 15% p95, error rate > 2x baseline, quality regression beyond configurable threshold).
Approval gates available: auto (no approval), ops-required, and manual-approve. Approval events are recorded in audit logs and linked to the rollout execution ID.
Simulated dry-run mode that replays production traffic through the proposed config in a shadow path without affecting responses and produces an evaluation report.

Operator can forcibly pause/resume or revert the rollout; these actions generate an incident ticket template in the Console and create a GitHub PR stub with the reverted config change for traceability.
tasks: Design controller protobufs and API surface for rollout objects (stages, thresholds, approvals).
Implement staged rollout state machine with timers and safe-advance checks.
Integrate metric collection hooks into runtime tracing for p50/p95 latency, token counts, cache hit rates, and model quality signals.
Build dry-run shadowing path and offline evaluator to calculate expected cost delta and quality delta.
Add approval workflow integration with SSO and Console UI (approve/deny/comment).
Create alerting rules and automated rollback playbook in Ops runbook format.
E2E tests: synthetic workload test, chaos (node failure) during rollout, and canary metrics regression injection.
decisions: Use deferred canaries (apply config to a shadowed subset of requests first, then small percent of live traffic) to reduce blast radius instead of immediate binary canaries.
Rollout phases: dry-run -> 1% -> 25% -> 100% to balance signal fidelity and safety.
Safety invariants selected: p95 latency, 30s tail latency, 5xx error delta, cache hit delta, and model quality regression measured by internal evals. Thresholds are configurable per-customer.
tradeoffs: Longer canary time improves safety but increases time-to-cost-savings. We default to conservative timers but allow customers to shorten windows via policy.
Shadow/dry-run adds runtime instrumentation complexity and additional storage for traced requests but avoids user-facing regressions.
Tighter rollback thresholds reduce false-positives but may block beneficial changes for noisy workloads; we expose per-customer sensitivity tuning.

notes: Prototype shows dry-run adds ~3-5% CPU overhead when sampling at 5% traffic; we'll gate sampling by customer tier to limit cost.
Ops asked for an 'escalation policy' hook to notify on-call with a summarized diff and direct link to rollback action.
Plan to ship alpha behind a feature flag and enable for internal beta customers only.
